name: Right Superior Vena Cava Connecting to Left-Sided Atrium
aliases: Right SVC to Left Atrium Connection
Anomalous Right Superior Vena Cava Drainage into Left Atrium

criteria.description: Identification of anomalous right superior vena cava drainage into the left atrium by echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI
Presence of unexplained central cyanosis or hypoxemia without pulmonary pathology
Positive contrast echocardiography bubble test demonstrating right-to-left shunting via the anomalous vessel
Exclusion of other intracardiac or extracardiac right-to-left shunts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed anomalous drainage plus clinical cyanosis or positive contrast bubble test
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on advanced cardiac imaging and exclusion of other causes of hypoxemia.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunt

searchTerms: low oxygen levels not improving with oxygen therapy
oxygen therapy failing to raise blood oxygen

common.symptomName: Paradoxical embolism leading to transient ischemic attacks

searchTerms: high red blood cell count from low oxygen
thick blood due to chronic hypoxia
increased blood cells from oxygen shortage

occasional.symptomName: Heart murmur due to turbulent flow

searchTerms: weakness on one side from embolism

rare.symptomName: Brain abscess due to septic emboli

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit and hemoglobin indicating secondary polycythemia
Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia with normal or low PaCO2
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating anomalous right SVC drainage into left atrium
Contrast-enhanced CT angiography or cardiac MRI confirming anomalous venous connection
Positive contrast bubble study showing right-to-left shunt
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; typically sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Exclusion of other causes of cyanosis and right-to-left shunts such as patent foramen ovale or pulmonary arteriovenous malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Left superior vena cava present instead of right
Drainage into coronary sinus rather than left atrium
May present with similar hypoxemia but different imaging findings

redFlags: Severe unexplained hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Neurological deficits suggestive of paradoxical embolism
Progressive cyanosis and clubbing in infancy or early childhood
references: Gatzoulis MA, et al. Anomalous systemic venous return to the left atrium: clinical presentation and management. Heart. 2000.
Warnes CA. Congenital anomalies of the systemic veins. Circulation. 2007.
